sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text: Venlo, on the German border, prices parking higher in the centre than around it and is tightening permits. The council decided the parking tax ordinance for 2026 on 7 November 2025: street parking in the centre costs 3.00 euros an hour on weekdays and 3.40 euros at weekends, with a day rate of 15.50 euros; in the surrounding Schil zone it costs 2.70 euros on weekdays, 3.10 at weekends and 13.40 euros a day; and the Rosarium area is day-ticket only at 19.50 euros [0]. Paid parking runs Monday to Wednesday and Friday to Saturday from 08:00 to 19:00, Thursday until 21:00 and, from 1 May 2026, Sunday from 12:00 to 19:00, where it ran from 08:00 until the end of April; the fine for not paying is 82.00 euros and wheel-clamping 185.72 euros [1]. The decree lists 2,109 street spaces in the paid zones and permit maximums of 1,878 resident permits, 187 seven-day business permits and 90 five-day business permits, with a waiting list once a cap is reached [2]. A first resident permit costs 163.20 euros a year in the centre and 88.80 euros in the Schil [4]. Addresses in the new Maasboulevard area and part of the Maaswaard area are designated 'GROP' addresses with no right to a street permit or a resident garage subscription, and new developments that raise parking pressure get no new street permits unless the municipality finds it necessary [3]. The parking-standards note for 2026, published on 16 June 2026 and valid to 2030, says parking is to be solved primarily on the developer's own site, with new home addresses getting no street or public-garage permit by default [18]. A letter of June 2025 describes a process towards regulated parking in the village core of Arcen, a proposal still under discussion [19].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: The question is where to put more parking. The temporary Arsenaal garage opened in April 2021, meets the centre's current demand according to a June 2025 council letter, and its concession lets it operate until April 2031 at the latest [14]. After a council amendment of January 2025 asking for a study of a municipal garage near Centrum-Oost aimed at 2029, the city reported in June 2025 that a 2021 study of an underground garage under the Julianapark was not financially sound, and launched two feasibility tracks: an update of that study, and an above-ground garage or mobility hub near the station that could also replace the Arsenaal and serve park-and-ride [15]. The measures already carried out include cashless parking, number-plate recognition for enforcement, a yearly parking-pressure survey and a longer paid window to 19:00, with better signage and dynamic guidance still planned and a resident poll on extending regulated parking scheduled for autumn 2025 [12]. After the council adopted the Mobiliteitsplan on 29 January 2025, the city used motorway information and traffic marshals on Good Friday and Easter Sunday 2025 to spread visitors [13]. Earlier charging concessions produced a network of 243 charging posts for greater Venlo, and a traffic decision of April 2026 would reserve two bays at each of 32 new posts, to be carried out after the objection period [16][17].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
Q-Park lists six garages in Venlo, Arsenaal (260 spaces), Blok van Gendt (200), Centrum Maasboulevard (535), Maaswaard (394), Nolensplein (745) and Roermondsepoort (528), all open round the clock, plus the P+R Stationsplein; tariffs did not load on its pages [8]. They have 68 charge points together [9]. Resident garage subscriptions are available only in Blok van Gendt, Nolensplein, Maaswaard, Arsenaal and Roermondsepoort [7]. Q-Park took over Maaswaard, Roermondsepoort and Nolensplein from the municipality in 2018 [11]. The P+R at Kaldenkerkerweg has 110 spaces, round-the-clock access and a discount for rail travellers [10].

Our data cover that park-and-ride, with 110 spaces, for about 50 days since 22 August 2026. Occupancy averaged about 24% on weekdays and 29% at weekends, with a peak of 88% on a Saturday afternoon, so it is busier at weekends than on workdays, which fits shoppers more than commuters. The garages in the centre are not in our data.
